nodes.name: POSTGRES 17
nodes.note: System of record. Two migration owners: Drizzle (apps/api/drizzle) runs first, then the OCR service's raw SQL — document.engagement_id FKs into tax_engagement.

nodes.name: REDIS
nodes.note: Three uses: idempotency locks, the case-queue cache with a generation counter, and per-tenant rate limiting.

nodes.name: DYNAMODB
nodes.note: Case-queue read model projection. Absent config degrades the endpoint to 503 rather than failing the boot.

nodes.name: S3 / LOCALSTACK
nodes.note: Document blobs at tenants/{t}/engagements/{e}/{uuid4} — the key carries no filename and no identifiers.

edges.note: CROSS-BOUNDARY WRITE. insert_audit_entry writes straight into Core's audit_entry table — no API call — matching Core's engagement:{id} target format so Core's audit endpoint picks it up. Shared database, not a contract.

CROSS-BOUNDARY READ. find_engagement_tenant SELECTs tenant_id FROM tax_engagement — a table Core owns and migrates. document.engagement_id also carries a real FK into it, which is why Drizzle migrations must run before the OCR ones.
S2-TV-029. Boots BOTH services for real against one Postgres and one RS256 keypair, nothing stubbed, then walks upload → attach → missing-list until the list is empty.
Pact consumer side. Pins the request shape Core sends; the provider side verifies it in the OCR service's own suite.
Pact provider verification. Constrains SHAPE only and fabricates the document row — which is exactly the gap the S2-TV-029 end-to-end test exists to close.

flows.label: 1 · UPLOAD
flows.blurb: Client posts a document to the OCR service. The blob lands in S3 before the row lands in Postgres, and a failed insert compensates the blob.

steps.label: multipart in
steps.note: FastAPI app; /v1 prefix is applied once at the mount so the router path cannot drift.

steps.label: size gate
steps.note: Refuses an oversized Content-Length before Starlette spools the body to disk.

steps.label: route
steps.note: Wiring only — verb + path to a controller method. AGENTS.md rule 10.

steps.label: Depends graph
steps.note: Built lazily per request, which is why /health boots without a database.

steps.label: verify RS256
steps.note: iss tax-vault-api, aud tax-vault-clients. The public key is captured once at module scope.

steps.label: service
steps.note: Owns the ordering: size cap → empty → content-type → doc_type → ROLE → tenant. The role check runs before any DB read so a rejected caller cannot tell 403 from 404.

steps.label: find_engagement_tenant
steps.note: SELECT tenant_id FROM tax_engagement — reading a table the Core service owns.

steps.label: build_key + put
steps.note: Key is tenants/{t}/engagements/{e}/{uuid4} — no filename, no identifiers.

steps.label: put_object
steps.note: The blob is written BEFORE the row. A failed insert compensates with a delete; a failed COMMIT deliberately does not, because the outcome is ambiguous.

steps.label: INSERT … RETURNING
steps.note: Then COMMIT. 201 with the new document id.

flows.label: 2 · ATTACH
flows.blurb: Core attaches the uploaded document: guards, then a cross-service HTTP hop into the OCR service with the caller's own token, then a single Drizzle transaction that writes the extraction and its audit entry together.

steps.label: rate limit
steps.note: Limit key is derived from the JWT tenant_id, not the IP.

steps.label: INCR
steps.note: Fails closed — no Redis means no writes.

steps.label: auth + role
steps.note: Auth and role both run BEFORE idempotency: a replay must not return stored fields to a caller the write path would have refused.

steps.label: canAttachDocuments ✓
steps.note: ATTACH_ROLES mirrors the OCR service's UPLOAD_ROLES: Firm Admin and Tax Preparer.

steps.label: lock
steps.note: Key is sha256(tenantId:METHOD URL:clientKey). Only the row id is cached — never the extracted fields.

steps.label: findById
steps.note: Tenant-scoped. A miss is a 404 before any stage logic runs.

steps.label: stage gate ✓
steps.note: The engagement must be in the Documents stage; otherwise the service audits the failure and throws DocumentStageRequiredError → 409.

steps.label: CROSS-SERVICE
steps.note: The caller's Authorization header is forwarded verbatim so the OCR service verifies the same principal against the same issuer. 3 attempts, exponential backoff with full jitter, per-attempt AbortSignal.timeout. 4xx never retries.

steps.label: verify again
steps.note: Ingestion re-verifies the token independently — it does not trust the hop.

steps.label: mock OCR
steps.note: assign_doc_type maps content-type to doc type: PDF→W-2, PNG→1099-INT, JPEG→K-1, else Other. Field values are hard-coded synthetic — no taxpayer identifiers by design.

steps.label: one txn
steps.note: update_document_doc_type, insert_succeeded_ocr_job, replace_extracted_fields, insert_audit_entry — then COMMIT. A Pydantic ValidationError instead quarantines the job and returns 422.

steps.label: INSERT ×N
steps.note: Includes a row in Core's audit_entry table — written directly, not through an API.

steps.label: zod-validated
steps.note: extractedDocumentSchema.parse runs before the payload enters Core. A mismatched engagement_id is a 409 — Ingestion owns that link.

steps.label: same txn
steps.note: The audit append shares the transaction, so the engagement can never carry attached fields the trail does not record.

steps.label: UPSERT
steps.note: ON CONFLICT (ingestion_document_id) DO UPDATE … setWhere taxEngagementId = :id. The setWhere is what makes a cross-engagement re-attach return zero rows and surface as a 409.

flows.label: 3 · MISSING LIST
flows.blurb: The checklist read: required doc types minus the distinct doc types already attached. This is the endpoint the S2-TV-029 end-to-end test drives to zero.

steps.label: role gate
steps.note: canReadMissingDocuments. Role runs before the handler so a forbidden caller cannot probe which engagements exist by comparing 403 against 404. A Client-role token gets 403.

steps.label: checklist
steps.note: Seeded inside the create transaction, so every engagement has its required rows from birth.

steps.label: attached
steps.note: SELECT DISTINCT doc_type FROM extracted_document, engagement-scoped.

flows.label: POST /v1/auth/login
flows.blurb: First factor only. A correct password returns 202 and a short-lived MFA token — never a session.

steps.label: 202 + MFA token
steps.note: Deliberately not an access token. The session only exists after the TOTP challenge succeeds.

flows.label: POST /v1/auth/mfa/challenge
flows.blurb: Second factor. A valid TOTP mints the RS256 access token that every other endpoint — and the OCR service — verifies.

steps.label: TOTP verify
steps.note: Secrets are sealed with AES-256-GCM at rest and the response carries Cache-Control: no-store.

steps.label: 200 tokens
steps.note: RS256, iss tax-vault-api, aud tax-vault-clients — the same trust the Python verifier is built against.

flows.label: POST /v1/engagements
flows.blurb: Creates the case for one (client × tax year) and seeds its required-document checklist in the same transaction.

steps.label: seed checklist
steps.note: Same transaction — an engagement without its checklist would report an empty missing-list forever.

steps.label: INSERT ×2
steps.note: A duplicate (tenant, client, year) surfaces as 409 via the Postgres unique violation.

flows.label: PATCH /v1/engagements/:id/stage
flows.blurb: Advances the six-stage machine and projects the result into the DynamoDB case queue.

steps.label: stage machine
steps.note: Intake → Documents → Preparation → Review → Filed → Archived. Backward and skipped transitions are refused; on_hold preserves the resume stage.

steps.label: invalidate
steps.note: Generation-counter fence, so a slow read cannot resurrect a stale queue after the write.

flows.label: GET /v1/case-queue
flows.blurb: Redis-cached read over the DynamoDB projection. Unconfigured DynamoDB degrades to 503 instead of failing the boot.

steps.label: GET
steps.note: A miss coalesces concurrent callers onto one Dynamo query rather than stampeding.

flows.label: GET /v1/engagements/:id/audit
flows.blurb: The append-only trail. Database triggers reject UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE, and the OCR service writes into this same table.

steps.label: SELECT
steps.note: Rows here come from BOTH services — Core writes engagement.document.attach, the OCR service writes document.ocr.extract.
